sections.title: Objective type questions: each has two parts of 1 mark.

questions.q: Define environmental stress.
questions.answer: An undesirable transaction between the person and the environment.

questions.q: Name the three models of human–environment relationship.
questions.answer: Humans subjugated to nature, humans control over nature, and symbiotic relationship.

questions.q: Define pollution.
questions.answer: An undesirable change in the physical, chemical or biological characteristics of air, land and water that may harm life.

questions.q: Name the five types of environmental stressors.
questions.answer: Air pollution, water pollution, noise pollution, crowding and greenhouse effect.

questions.q: Name any two major air pollutants.
questions.answer: Carbon dioxide, nitrogen oxide, sulphur dioxide, suspended particulates including lead (any two).

questions.q: Name any two sources of water pollution.
questions.answer: Domestic waste water, industrial waste water, agricultural run-off (any two).

questions.q: Differentiate density and crowding in one line each.
questions.answer: Density is the objective number of persons per unit area; crowding is the subjective feeling of discomfort.

questions.q: Define sustainable development.
questions.answer: Development that meets the needs of the present without compromising the ability of future generations to meet their own needs.

questions.q: Differentiate want and need in one line each.
questions.answer: A want is a wishful desire without end; a need is something essential for survival.

sections.title: Objective type questions: each has four parts of 1 mark.

questions.q: Name the model: (i) nature is worshipped; (ii) science and technology dominate; (iii) interdependence; (iv) which model recognises our limitations?
questions.answer: (i) Humans subjugated to nature. (ii) Humans control over nature. (iii) Symbiotic. (iv) Symbiotic relationship.

questions.q: Identify the effect: (i) hearing loss; (ii) disrupted communication; (iii) pick-pocketing in rush hour; (iv) rising sea level.
questions.answer: (i) Noise pollution. (ii) Noise pollution. (iii) Crowding. (iv) Greenhouse effect (global warming).

questions.q: Name four ways to help the environment.
questions.answer: Conserve water; use public transport; plant trees; reduce, reuse and recycle; save electricity (any four).

questions.q: Name four effects of crowding.
questions.answer: Crime, aggression, raised blood pressure, social withdrawal, learned helplessness (any four).

sections.title: Very short answer questions. Answer in 30–50 words.

questions.q: What is environment?
questions.answer: The physical world and the social and cultural surroundings in which we live and interact.

questions.q: What is the symbiotic view?
questions.answer: Humans and nature are interdependent; neither is self-sufficient and humans must not exploit nature blindly.

questions.q: Name two health effects of air pollution.
questions.answer: Respiratory problems, asthma, cardiovascular problems, eye problems, early deaths (any two).

questions.q: Why do people habituate to noise?
questions.answer: Familiarity and attitude reduce annoyance so they feel less discomfort over time.

questions.q: Why does crowding differ in a marriage party and an overcrowded bus?
questions.answer: Density may be equal but the relationship with people, duration and meaning differ, so experience differs.

questions.q: What is the greenhouse effect?
questions.answer: Gases such as carbon dioxide, methane and CFCs trap the sun's heat in the atmosphere, raising temperature.

questions.q: Why is wasteful consumption a worry for sustainability?
questions.answer: It depletes non-renewable and renewable resources, leaving little for future generations.

sections.title: Short answer questions. Answer in 50–80 words.

questions.q: Explain the models of human–environment relationship.
questions.answer: Subjugation: nature rules humans and is worshipped; control: science and technology dominate nature but bring global warming and ozone loss; symbiotic: interdependence, duty to nature and avoiding blind exploitation.

questions.q: Describe air pollution and its sources.
questions.answer: An imbalance in air quality due to gases and particulates; sources are power consumption, industry, vehicles, burning refuse, smoking and cutting trees.

questions.q: Describe the ill effects of noise pollution.
questions.answer: Health hazards (sleeplessness, irritability, hearing loss), aggression and less helping behaviour, disrupted communication, lower performance and accidents.

questions.q: Explain the effects of crowding.
questions.answer: Crowding increases crime, causes violence in prisons and psychiatric institutions, raises blood pressure and heart rate and causes anger, aggression, withdrawal and learned helplessness.

questions.q: Explain the greenhouse effect and its consequences.
questions.answer: Carbon dioxide, methane and CFCs trap heat, causing global warming, melting ice caps, rising sea levels, storms, flooding and agricultural disruption.

questions.q: How can an individual contribute to a better environment?
questions.answer: By conserving water and electricity, using public transport and cloth bags, composting, recycling, planting trees and buying energy-efficient appliances.

sections.title: Long answer questions. Answer in 80–120 words.

questions.q: Explain any one model of human–environment relationship and the concept of environmental stress.
questions.answer: Environmental stress is an undesirable person–environment transaction. In the symbiotic model, humans and nature are interdependent; blind exploitation of resources like oil and coal causes pollution and threats, so balance and duty to nature are needed.

questions.q: Describe air pollution and its consequences for health.
questions.answer: Air pollution is imbalance in air quality due to gases and particulates from power use, industry, vehicles, burning and tree cutting. It causes irritation, respiratory and cardiovascular disease, hypertension, asthma, neurological and visual problems and early death; Bhopal is an example.

questions.q: Describe water pollution, noise pollution and crowding.
questions.answer: Water pollution from domestic, industrial and agricultural waste causes diarrhoea and hepatitis. Noise pollution causes health problems, aggression, communication difficulty and accidents. Crowding is subjective discomfort that raises crime, aggression and illness.

questions.q: Discuss the greenhouse effect, sustainable development and the need for simple living.
questions.answer: Greenhouse gases cause global warming and rising seas; reversal needs fewer emissions, trees and banning CFCs. Sustainable development meets present needs without harming future generations. Distinguishing needs from wants and simple living reduce exploitation.
